idiom_name: private lock object with synchronized blocks; Ref for effect-based code
implementation_notes: Scala runs on the JVM, so the blocking guardian is a private lock instance with `synchronized` blocks around private state - `synchronized` on the enclosing instance is Java's Monitor Object, not this pattern - and the JVM supplies the monitor-enter/exit happens-before guarantee. The functional face of the same guarantee is a concurrent state cell: a `Ref` (cats-effect, ZIO) or a bare `AtomicReference` that exposes only atomic `get`/`modify`/`updateAndGet` operations, so the value is never handed out for unlocked mutation and no thread is ever blocked. Scala's standard library also ships `TrieMap`, a concurrent map whose compound updates are atomic - a ready-made guardian for map-shaped state - while `ReentrantReadWriteLock` covers the read-heavy case.
pitfalls: `synchronized` on `this` (or on any value that escapes the class) publishes the lock; the lock must be private and final, and Scala's implicit conversions make 'which object is this?' genuinely ambiguous for boxed/AnyVal receivers.
Blocking inside a `synchronized` block on an effect runtime's compute thread starves the whole pool; effect code must use its own `Ref`/`Semaphore` instead of JVM monitors.

A `var` captured by a closure is invisible to the compiler's concurrency checks: the guardian only works if the `var` is private and every access goes through the guarded methods, which Scala cannot enforce.

variants.name: Functional state cell (cats-effect Ref)
variants.implementation_notes: In effect-based Scala the guardian is a `Ref[F, A]`: the state is only reachable through `get`, `set`, `modify` and `updateAndGet`, which are atomic (the implementation is a functional wrapper over `AtomicReference`), so the serialisation point is a compare-and-set loop rather than a monitor and no thread is ever blocked. This is the form to use when the surrounding program is already in `IO`/`ZIO`: the update function is the guarded operation, and waiting for a condition is expressed with `Deferred`/`Semaphore` instead of a condition variable. Two documented limits matter - the cell must not hold mutable objects, because atomicity is by reference, and `Ref` alone provides no mutual exclusion for effects, so critical sections that must be exclusive across awaits need a semaphore as well.
pitfalls: `Ref` gives atomicity only for reference transitions: storing a mutable collection and mutating it in place escapes the cell's protection.
Two `Ref` updates are two atomic steps; a transaction over several cells needs `Ref` composition or STM, never two sequential updates assumed to be one.
